settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Security, sessions, nodes and their limits, display and export. Changes to security, nodes and limits ask for your password and authenticator code.
settings.unlock: Confirm it is you to show
settings.stepUp.reason: This change needs your password and your authenticator code.
settings.stepUp.totpShape: Enter the six digits your authenticator app shows.
settings.export.summary: Download an encrypted export, or import one into this installation.
settings.security.title: Security
settings.security.summary: Password, authenticator app and recovery codes.
settings.security.intro: Changing the password or the authenticator ends every other session. Each change asks for your current password and code first.
settings.security.passwordRule: At least 12 characters, with a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, a digit and a symbol.
settings.security.passwordMismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
settings.security.passwordChanged: Password changed. Every other session has ended.
settings.security.passwordReason: Changing the password needs your current password and your authenticator code.
settings.security.totpIntro: Replace the authenticator when you move to a new phone. The old one keeps working until the new one is confirmed.
settings.security.totpScan: Scan this code with the new authenticator app, or type the key below into it. Then enter the code it shows.
settings.security.totpQr: QR code of the new authenticator key
settings.security.totpExpires: This key must be confirmed before {time}.
settings.security.totpChanged: Authenticator replaced. Every other session has ended; log in with the new app from now on.
settings.security.totpReason: Replacing the authenticator needs your password and a code from the current authenticator.
settings.security.recoveryIntro: A recovery code lets you log in once without the authenticator, to set up a new one.
settings.security.recoveryConsequences: Ten new codes replace all the old ones at once: the old codes stop working. The new codes are shown only once.
settings.security.recoveryNew: Your new recovery codes. They are shown only now: download or write them down and keep them away from this device.
settings.security.recoveryReason: Recovery codes need your password and your authenticator code.
settings.sessions.title: Sessions and devices
settings.sessions.summary: Where you are logged in, known devices and session timeouts.
settings.sessions.intro: End a session you do not recognise, or log out everywhere. Known devices may log in without waiting after failed attempts elsewhere.
settings.sessions.revokeConsequences: That browser is logged out at once and its live updates stop.
settings.sessions.revokeCurrentConsequen: This browser is logged out at once; you will need to log in again.
settings.sessions.everywhereConsequences: Every session ends, this one too. Known devices stay known; remove them below if one is lost.
settings.sessions.devicesLocked: The list of known devices is shown after you confirm with your password and authenticator code.
settings.sessions.devicesIntro: Browsers that have logged in before. Removing one does not end its session; end that above.
settings.sessions.revokeDeviceConsequenc: The device is no longer known: after failed logins elsewhere it has to wait like any other browser. Its current session stays until it ends.
settings.sessions.devicesReason: Known devices need your password and your authenticator code.
settings.sessions.policyLocked: The timeouts are shown after you confirm with your password and authenticator code.
settings.sessions.idle: Log out after this long without activity
settings.sessions.absolute: Log out after this long in any case
settings.sessions.absoluteHint: Between 1 minute and 365 days, and not shorter than the time without activity.
settings.sessions.policyRange: Enter whole numbers within the ranges shown.
settings.sessions.policyOrder: The time without activity cannot be longer than the session's whole length.
settings.sessions.policySaved: Timeouts saved. Shorter timeouts apply to sessions already open; longer ones only to new sessions.
settings.sessions.policyReason: Session timeouts need your password and your authenticator code.
settings.display.title: Display
settings.display.summary: View, theme and number format on this device.
settings.display.intro: These choices are kept in this browser only. They change what is shown, never what is allowed.
settings.display.viewNote: Basic shows status, balances, channels, payments, pay and receive. Advanced shows everything.
settings.display.formatNote: Grouping and decimal marks follow a region. Tor Browser reports the same region for everyone, so choose yours here if the numbers look wrong.
settings.display.notSettings: The interface is in English; amounts are shown in sats. Other units, fiat values and languages come in a later release.
settings.nodes.title: Nodes
settings.nodes.summary.one: {count} node. Add, replace credentials, set limits.
settings.nodes.summary.other: {count} nodes. Add, replace credentials, set limits.
settings.nodes.intro: The Core Lightning nodes this app manages. Each one is reached over HTTPS with its own pinned certificate.
settings.nodes.emptyBody: Add a Core Lightning node: run the setup command on the node, then paste what it prints.
settings.access.read-only.help: Shows the node; can create invoices and addresses, but cannot spend.
settings.access.standard.help: Also pays, sends on-chain and opens and closes channels, within the app's limits.
settings.access.full.help: Standard, plus a few node settings (alias, colour, autoclean).
settings.node.commandIntro: Run this command on the node's host with lightning-cli and jq installed. It makes credentials limited to what this app needs and prints them as one block to paste below. It downloads nothing.
settings.node.name: Name in this app
settings.node.urlHint: An https:// address on this computer, the local network or Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10). Public addresses are refused.
settings.node.caHint: The ca.pem of clnrest. Only this certificate is trusted for this node; changing it later needs a replacement.
settings.node.serverNameHint: The name the node's certificate was issued for. clnrest uses localhost.
settings.node.credentialForm.block: Paste the block from the setup command
settings.node.credentialForm.runes: Enter the runes one by one
settings.node.credentialBlockHint: The JSON block the setup command printed. Keep it secret.
settings.node.adminWarning: An admin credential can reveal the node's secrets, create new credentials and spend around this app's limits if this server is ever compromised. Use it only if a restricted credential is not possible.
settings.node.adminAcknowledge: I understand the risk of an admin credential
settings.node.adminRequired: Confirm that you understand the risk of an admin credential first.
settings.node.readOnlyNote: A read-only node cannot spend, so it needs no spending limits now.
settings.node.invalid: Some values do not have the expected form. Check the address, the certificate and the credentials.
settings.node.limitsNeeded: This node can spend and has no limits yet. Set them below, then send again.
settings.node.checking: Connecting to the node and checking the credentials and the chain…
settings.node.reason: Changing a node's connection or credentials needs your password and your authenticator code.
settings.node.spendStatusNote: The view credential is checked now; the spend credential's state is from its last full check or the last refused spend.
settings.node.replaceIntro: Enter the whole connection again: address, certificate and credentials. The node must stay the same (same chain, network and public key).
settings.node.removeIntro: Its credentials are deleted. Its history and limits stay, and come back if the same node is added again.
settings.node.removeConsequences: This app stops managing the node and deletes its stored credentials. The node itself and its funds are not touched.
settings.node.removeBlocked: This node has spends whose outcome is not settled. Resolve them first.
settings.limits.title: Spending limits
settings.limits.intro: These limits apply only to spends made through Lightning Pilot, so a stolen session cannot drain the node. Payments made by other apps on the node are not limited.
settings.limits.scopeNote: Amounts in whole sats. Leave a cap empty for no cap.
settings.limits.noStepUp: Empty: never ask for the password because of the amount.
settings.limits.maxFeeSharePercent: Highest on-chain fee as a share of the amount (%)
settings.limits.maxRoutingFeeSharePercen: Highest routing fee as a share of the payment (%)
settings.limits.order: The password threshold cannot be above the single-spend cap, and the single-spend cap cannot be above the 24-hour cap.
settings.limits.invalid: Some values are not valid: whole sats, a fee rate with up to three decimals, and percentages from 0 to 100 (the on-chain share from 1).
settings.limits.none: This node has no limits yet, so it cannot spend through Lightning Pilot. Save limits to allow it.
settings.limits.feeShareNote: Limits are shared by every entry for the same node (same chain and public key).
settings.limits.reason: Changing limits needs your password and your authenticator code.
settings.spends.title: Unresolved spends
settings.spends.summary: Spends whose outcome the node has not confirmed.
settings.spends.intro: Lightning Pilot keeps asking the node and settles these by itself when the node knows. Mark one by hand only when you have checked the node yourself.
settings.spends.emptyBody: When the node does not confirm whether a payment, send or channel action went through, it appears here until it is settled.
settings.spends.interrupted: The server stopped while the node was working on it.
settings.spends.unclear: The node's answer did not say whether it went through.
settings.spends.succeededMeans: The spend keeps counting against the limits, as money that left the node.
settings.spends.failedMeans: The spend stops counting against the limits.
settings.spends.broadcast: The node's wallet lists this transaction, so it was sent. It can only be marked as sent.
settings.spends.reason: Settling a spend by hand needs your password and your authenticator code.
